english_restorations.basis: Restores the 'rich' member of the rich/poor antithetical naming pair, with the repeated naming verb introducing the second member that follows ('some others poor').

Renders the proposed ⲍⲁⲧⲉⲍⲏ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲙⲡⲁ[ⲧⲉ] formula that organizes every other paragraph of the teaching. Low confidence reflects that this is a true 16-char lacuna whose restoration is structural rather than visible.

restoration_note: The teaching is structured by the recurring rhetorical formula ⲍⲁⲧⲉⲍⲏ/ϩⲁⲧⲉϩⲏ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲙⲡⲁⲧⲉ ('beforehand, before...') introducing each station of regeneration that the Lord has prepared in advance: separation of day from night, sending of the Third Ambassador to the outer watch, adornment of the ships of light by the Father of Life, dispatch of the Judge to discriminate the radiant from the destroyed, sending of Christ against Error, the naming of human conditions (rich/poor), the appointment of stars and spheres for births and judgment, the releasers preparing the loosing of the cosmos, and finally the Great Builder/First Architect summoned to build the new Aeon. Most gaps are short letter-completions of words whose other letters survive on the line, so character count and parallel formulae fix them with high confidence. Gap 14 follows the editor's antithetical-naming reconstruction with moderate confidence. Gap 15 is the only true 16-char lacuna; the structural adverb ⲍⲁⲧⲉⲍⲏ ⲁⲛ ⲉⲙⲡⲁ[ⲧⲉ] fits both the surrounding rhetorical pattern and the visible -ⲧⲉ trailing the gap, but is marked low because no parallel binds it absolutely.
